Nadia Flores: Quick follow-up on compaction: propose a "budgeted runner" that enforces both time and page limits per epoch, plus a tiny cost model to avoid cross-pool thrash.
Tom H.: Budgeted epochs make sense. How do we keep the cost model cheap?
Nadia Flores: Keep cost linear: cost_move = size_bytes/est_bw + pcie_latency + cpu_copy_units. Benefit = sampled_fault_count * avg_fault_cost. Move if benefit * profit_factor > cost_move. No heavy ML.
Laura Chen: How to protect high-SLO tenants?
Nadia Flores: Two knobs: per-tenant defrag_priority in allocation metadata, and a global SLO detector that reduces budgets if tail latency spikes. Runner reads priority off allocation descriptor, not on hot path.
Ibrahim Khan: Hotness tracking? per-page counters will be heavy.
Nadia Flores: Use 1% sampling of accesses to update a tiny EMA per-page, plus a small bloom-like hotset. Cheap memory and CPU.
Tom H.: Correctness around migrating pages and DMA completions?
Nadia Flores: Use indirection header (ptr, seq) and retire-list: old page marked RETIRING with retire_epoch = cur_epoch + hold. Default hold=1 epoch which covers late DMA. Readers check seq before/after access; if odd or changed, retry.
Laura Chen: What about forced reclaim when pressure hits?
Nadia Flores: If retired_ratio exceeds max_retired_ratio or memory pressure high, runner allows forced_reclaim that zeroes and fences pages before return; increment reclaimed_under_pressure counter and alert if frequent.
Ibrahim Khan: Rollout plan? metrics to add?
Nadia Flores: Phase 1 lab canary: epoch_ms=50, pages_limit=256, retire_hold=1. Metrics: retired_pages, retired_ratio, header_retry_rate, move_cost_estimate_hist, reclaimed_under_pressure_count, p95_token_latency. Phase 2 perf on embedding workloads.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary "budgeted-compact-v1" on lab-node-2 :eyes:
Tom H.: I'll help with cost calibration and telemetry labels.
Laura Chen: I'll own the runner prototype and tests.
Nadia Flores: Thanks! Will open WIP PR with small diagram and sim harness.
